answer: Because the orchard ledger attributes every share, the pigment audit exposes the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. Only 50% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not pay. A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, which means it forfeits the quill fee twice and still divides one payout. That is 33 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
